content: Some women who experience threatened preterm labor may stabilize and subsequently be prescribed oral tocolytic maintenance therapy, such as betamimetics, to prevent preterm birth and prolong pregnancy. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of oral betamimetic maintenance therapy in preventing preterm birth following an episode of threatened preterm labor. The search for relevant studies was updated on November 9, 2012, using the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register. The inclusion criteria focused on randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared oral betamimetics with alternative tocolytic therapies, placebo, or no treatment for maintenance therapy after threatened preterm labor. Two independent reviewers applied the selection criteria, extracted data, and assessed the quality of the included studies. The updated search did not identify any new trials, so the results remain unchanged from the previous review. A total of 13 RCTs involving 1551 women were included in the analysis. When comparing betamimetics with placebo, no significant differences were observed in the rates of admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) (risk ratio [RR] 1.28, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.68 to 2.41; two RCTs involving 2600 women treated with terbutaline). Similarly, no significant differences were found when comparing betamimetics with magnesium sulfate (RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.43 to 1.46; one RCT involving 137 women). The rate of preterm birth before 37 weeks of gestation also showed no significant difference. This outcome was assessed in six RCTs, four of which compared ritodrine with placebo or no treatment, and two of which compared terbutaline with placebo or no treatment (RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.35; 644 women). Additionally, no differences were observed between betamimetics and placebo, no treatment, or other tocolytic therapies in terms of perinatal mortality and morbidity outcomes. However, adverse effects such as tachycardia were reported more frequently in women receiving betamimetics compared to those in the placebo, no treatment, or alternative tocolytic groups. In conclusion, the available evidence does not support the use of oral betamimetics as maintenance therapy following threatened preterm labor.
